validity.recommendation: An independent Penza Oblast MChS government document states that Petrovsk-Elets consists of TWO 1220mm pipes with a COMBINED throughput of 45 million m3/day (~16.4 bcm/y) -- i.e. 16.4 bcm/y is explicitly a two-pipe SYSTEM total, not a per-pipe figure. GEM carries P1466 ('Petrovsk-Elets') at Capacity=16.40 AND a sibling row P5656 ('Petrovsk-Elets Looping'/expansion) also at Capacity=16.40 (per prior-session CSV check). If P1466 and P5656 represent the system's two separate physical pipes, then recording the FULL combined 16.40 on BOTH rows double-counts total system capacity as ~32.8 bcm/y, roughly double the true ~16.4 bcm/y combined throughput. Recommend a human reviewer check whether P5656 should instead carry a per-pipe or incremental-looping capacity value distinct from P1466's, per this batch's flagged 'Petrovsk-Algasovo-Elets SYSTEM aggregate-vs-segment concern'.

fills.researcher_notes: IMPORTANT DUPLICATE/SPEC CONCERN -- see validity[] and cross_row_leads[]. The MChS source explicitly describes 45 million m3/day (~16.4 bcm/y) as the COMBINED throughput of BOTH pipes ('две трубы... производительностью 45 млн куб. м в сутки' -- two pipes, [combined] output 45 million m3/day), not per-pipe. GEM's sibling row P5656 ('Petrovsk-Elets Looping'/expansion pipeline) ALSO carries Capacity=16.40 per the prior session's CSV check. If each row is meant to represent ONE of the two physical pipes, then EITHER (a) each row should carry roughly half the combined figure (~8.2 bcm/y) with the 16.40 being the two-pipe system total, or (b) 16.40 is correct for the system and one of the two rows is double-counting it. Filing this value as recorded (REFS_ADDED, matches the sheet) because the aggregate 16.4 IS what the source states and is not itself wrong, but flagging strongly that having BOTH P1466 and P5656 independently carry the full combined 16.40 figure looks like a double-count error requiring human adjudication.
